title: CRASH-139: zend api read property stack member zval nonowned literal string freed by userland arg stack (invalid-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:global-buffer-overflow at Zend/zend_alloc.c:263 in _efree when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 9a98904ddd0e, which postdates the release, and names the defect at Zend/zend_API.c:1957 + :1965 + :1966
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has _efree at Zend/zend_alloc.c:263 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites
